comment: Dr. Curtis is so sweet and really cares about her students both in academics and apart from that. Her class is basically AP Statistics and some Excel assignments. Everything is super easy if you go over the notes and understand the formulas. Very little homework as well which is nice! Exams weight a lot but are just like the practice exams.

Very accessible out of class but won't explain the material to you in a different way. If you don't get it her way then you're out of luck since that is the only way that will be explained to you. Textbook is also expensive. Take someone else if you can.
super densed class with tons of mateirals. she has her favorites in class and treats students differently

Dr. Curtis is great, but BSTATS is inherently challenging for those without a solid foundation in math. She speaks quickly, but you get used to it. Offers a lot of extra credit and exams are not very difficult, very similar to practice problems. Very flexible and very caring.

Very enthusiastic with clear, organised lecture notes which are used for all teaching. Would recommend using digital lecture notes on an iPad to write on rather than printing if possible. Very expensive digital textbook which is pointless apart from for mandatory homeworks. Easy with any stats or math background but likely confusing otherwise.
Expensive textbook, boring lectures. I agree with other reviews saying she's biased. Nice to people that she likes. Two faced and horrible person.

Class is an easy A if you pay attention and do all the homework. Homeworks are easy A's and don't take long. She slows down in class if students need clarity, and all tests have cheat sheets. The textbook is pretty expensive, so for that reason, I would recommend a different B-stat teacher, but otherwise, she's a good teacher.
The content really isn't the most interesting, but she does a good job of teaching it. Not a bad experience at all, just nothing to write home about. Average foundational b-school class.

This class is definitely easier if you have at least some minor idea of stats (or if you are willing to learn). Dr. Curtis is seriously one of the nicest people in the business school. She takes such care to learn everyone's names and is so enthusiastic. An A is verrryyyyy do-able if you do the HW and study just an average amount for the tests.
Don't take her! Take either Dr. Orr or Arnold if you can

if you don't understand anything about math (like me) this class will be quite difficult, but still feasible to get a good grade in. dr curtis is very kind and always willing to help out, even after class hours. the class requires a lot of work and you def have to review your notes frequently, but if you work hard, you will do well.

If you don't have any stats experience the lectures will be hard to follow. Homework makes up a significant part of the grade with two midterms and a final. She's a nice professor, but classes are basically only lectures and can get boring.

Professor Curtis is an effective teacher that covers an accelerated course well. The nature of the class demands a fast-paced lecture type class environment which can be difficult for students with no background in statistics. The exams are somewhat tougher than the in-class problems but she gives you previous years' exams to help prepare.

I would come back here again and again to complain how awful of a person she is. I am literally still traumatized from her class and how she treated me. In one of her emails, she literally insinuated being sick is my problem. But if she likes you, she could be the sweetest prof you would ever meet at UR. If not, I wish you all the best

Curtis is such a sweet lady but the class is difficult. I'm not good at statistics but her kindness always encouraged me to go to class. Tests makeup 65% of your grade while HW/Excel is 35%. She is probably the best bstats/econ170 teacher at Richmond which tbf isn't saying much. I would recommend this class over any other bstats course at Richmond.

This was the hardest class I taken in college so far. I had no background with stats and the class felt extremely difficult. I found it hard to conceptually understand her explanations. If you don't have any experience take a different prof! However, the grade distribution was good, homework (an easy 100) is ~35% of the grade (over one midterm).

Prof. Curtis is caring about her students, she wants everyone to do well. Her lectures are very fast paced, and can be confusing if you get lost. She is responsive to questions during class and she will go over steps again if you miss them. There is a LOT of outside homework on Cengage, but the class prepares you well for the competency exam.
Need to buy expensive Cengage account and class can be difficult with no prior statistics experience, but for students ready for B-stat she is a good option.
She is good lecturer. And stats are somehow confusing but as long as you follow her steps you will be fine.

Curtis is selectively nice to people, which I experienced during her office hours. Her behaviors impacted my mental health so much that I had to go see CAPS. Her emails were also passive-aggressive and rude to some students. The class is tough without a coding background, but my friends with prior comp science experience did very well.
You have to buy a $130 cengage account. Horrible professor and teaching style.

She is very kind and great for BStats but awful for MATH329. This was the most disorganized and confusing course I have taken in my 3 years here because of Dr. Curtis (when it really shouldn't be), and I did not learn much at all. She is not qualified to teach the course and luckily is not going to next year.

Curtis is so sweet and she does a great job explaining abstract concepts. I considered bstats difficult because the class covers ALOT of content and there will be many many formulas to memorize but I don't think you can blame the professor for that. It's just the subject. Got a B and I'm bad at math, if you are good at math you will be fine.

If you're looking to take bstats you should definitely go for Dr. Curtis. Contents may get harder towards the second half of the semester but she is super caring and helpful during office hours. Workload is not large and grades fairly.

Dr. Curtis is so nice and caring. The class is pretty fast paced, but she does a good job of structuring it. 70% of your grade is close to bi-weekly problem sets which can be difficult at times. Two midterms and final, 10% each, and they are all take home and open note. Dr. Curtis is really passionate about teaching and it shows, take her.

Huyen is the kindest prof at UR. She can be a little confusing at times but she is helpful in office hours. Gives moderately difficult but fair exams. If you study, you should be fine. She assigns online Cengage homework with 3 attempts to get right, so you should have ~100% for homework. 3 exams and a couple of Excel assignments for the semester.

If you know python, this will make your experience a lot easier. Tons of material is learned over a short period of time, you shouldn't miss lectures even though they are recorded. My only complaint is that somebody else grades the homework assignments and doesn't mark why the questions are wrong, only that 5 points are docked.
Dr. Curtis is so good

I took Econ 170 with doctor Curtis and she is a very intelligent teacher who makes an effort for each student to understand the course material. The class is fast-paced and if you lose focus during class or miss homework you can fall behind. Overall great class for people interested in math.

I took AP Statistics in high school and got a 5. I was excited to take this class, but I can now say I am more confused than when it began. Professor Curtis is a very nice woman but makes simple concepts extremely confusing. That being said, the class is relatively easy, and an A is attainable if you put in some level of effort.

I have absolutely no idea what is going on in this class. I have received good grades on all assignments and tests, yet I have learned nothing. This class teaches you how to figure out a way to get by without knowing anything. Curtis cares about her students but does not do a good job educating her students.

Curtis is a really nice woman, she really cares about her students and wants them to learn, but I find that she makes frequent mistakes in class. I took stats in HS, and I found that her way of explaining things made previously familiar subjects super confusing. It's not a hard class, but she just doesn't really make things all that clear.

Prof Curtis is so nice and really cares about her students. Homework grades are almost equal to 2 full test grades, and you are almost guaranteed to get a 100 on the homeworks (multiples attempts). The only thing I found annoying about this class was that other BUAD classes seemed MUCH easier (online tests, cheat sheets), which made it seem unfair.

I feel like a lot of these comments aren't really fair to Dr. Curtis. She has her own style for lectures, which can definitely be confusing at times. But if you email her or go to office hours, she'll work with you until you get it, and she isn't judgmental when you ask questions. She's a fair grader, but you'll have to work hard in the class.

Professor Curtis was great in class and online she was always very energetic about class and happy to be there. There are a lot of HW assignments which aren't too bad, there's just a lot. Make sure you come to class if you miss one you will miss lots as class goes quickly and lots its covered. I would recommend her for BUAD 202 though.

Professor Curtis is a kind woman who truly cares about her students. While the subject matter isn't very interesting, she does her best to give us relevant examples. She is extremely knowledgable, but can sometimes over-explain concepts, which ultimately makes it more confusing. She is flexible and the language barrier has minimal impact.

I will be honest. I found Professor Curtis to be condescending in her emails. But then when I came to her office hours, she was very nice. I think it might be due to language that we might perceive her to be more condescending than she is in real life. Professor Curtis hw every week, but you can practice for exam. NEVER SKIP HER CLASS.

Prof Curtis means well and does an okay job summarizing the textbook and teaching it in a neater way. However, the amount of homework was generally excessive and I found her a little condescending at times when asking for help. Shes not too brutal on grading, but youre definitely going to have to put some work in to get an A or even a B+

Enjoyed the class while on campus, but struggled greatly once everything was switched over online. Her exams are very challenging and she can be a tough grader with homework assignments. Not a bad Stats professor, but would not recommend for an online course.

Professor Curtis is a very nice person, but not a great professor for an intro stats class. I have taken stats in high school, and I became more confused about stuff i once found easy after taking her class. She is extremely picky when grading, and exams can be tough. Lots of homework was assigned when classes went online. Wouldn't take again.

She is a great professor and wonderful persons. Her tests are not that difficult and she gives you partial credit on problems you try on your tests. She is also available many times a week for additional help.

Dr. Curtis is very enthusiastic. She explains everything well and clearly. Gives a fair amount of homework so that you can understand the concepts better. Her tests are long but they're not hard. Pay attention and take good notes in class, do the homework and you will be fine. She is very helpful during office hours so take advantage of that.
Nice enthusiastic teacher. However, you need to attend every class. I know kids in other bstats classes and I can say that Prof Curtis is one of the easiest one

Nice person; very helpful in office hour. Her class is not even hard and the materials in textbook were already simplified by her to be brought into the lecture. All you need to do is go to class, do the hw and study for the tests/ quizzes. Also, she explains and illustrates concepts very well. If you fail her class, you just didn't try enough.

DrCurtis is such a very nice professor. She puts a lot of enthusiasm into her lectures and always tries to ask if students understand or not. Her tests demand a thorough understanding of practical problems, but she is a fair grader. She has about more than 10 homework, but they have clear guideline, and she is accessible outside of class too.
